title: Government asks social media to remove videos of driving on the wrong side
seoTitle: Social platforms must delete dangerous driving videos
subtitle: Prime Minister says sharing reckless driving footage is reprehensible
excerpt: The government has asked TikTok and other platforms to remove videos of drivers traveling the wrong way. The Prime Minister condemned the sharing of such material.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The government has formally requested that social media platforms, including TikTok and other industry players, remove videos showing drivers traveling against traffic. The Prime Minister’s statement classifies the sharing of footage that depicts dangerous driving as a truly reprehensible act.

The role of digital platforms in public safety

The debate over content moderation on digital platforms involves the responsibility of tech companies in spreading risky behavior. Social networks use reporting systems and automatic detection algorithms to identify posts that violate safety guidelines. Cooperation between government agencies and technology firms is a common practice to curb the spread of material that could encourage violations or endanger citizens on public roads.

Risks associated with dangerous driving

Driving against traffic poses a serious threat to road safety, with the potential to cause severe head‑on collisions. Awareness of the dangers of reckless driving and the importance of staying attentive and respecting traffic rules are essential for preserving lives. Recording and publishing dangerous maneuvers online can have a negative impact, promoting conduct that threatens the physical integrity of drivers, passengers and pedestrians.

Removal requests and digital responsibility

Requests to take down specific content arise when it is understood that keeping the material online could cause collective harm or encourage hazardous practices. Tech companies evaluate these demands against their own terms of service and community guidelines, seeking to balance information flow with safety preservation.

Traffic education and digital awareness are key pillars in the information age. Displaying traffic violations as entertainment can distort risk perception, especially among audiences that consume short‑form video content. Efforts to discourage such publications involve not only direct moderation actions but also promoting ethical digital behavior among social media users.

With information from BBC News.
